seo.description: Si Datu Bua, Silolona Sojourns' 40m phinisi by Seery Yacht Design: three king suites for six guests and a crew of 15, chartered whole across Eastern Indonesia.

tagline: The Beloved Princess: three king suites, fifteen crew, and Eastern Indonesia chartered whole
answer: Si Datu Bua, "Beloved Princess", is Silolona Sojourns' newest phinisi: 40.2 metres, designed by Seery Yacht Design and built by the Konjo boat builders of Sulawesi. She has three king suites for six adults, with child beds possible in every cabin, and a crew of 15. She is chartered whole, in Komodo, Flores and Alor from May to September and Raja Ampat, Papua and Banda from October to April.
facts: By the Konjo master boat builders of Sulawesi; launch year not published
3 king suites: Banda, Toraja and Celebes
overview: Si Datu Bua, "Beloved Princess", is Silolona Sojourns' newest traditional sailing ship, designed by Seery Yacht Design and built by the master Konjo boat builders of Sulawesi. She is 40.2 metres overall with an 8.5 metre beam and cruises at 10 knots.

She carries only three cabins, each a king suite named for part of Indonesia: Banda, the master at 6.8 by 5.6 metres, and Toraja and Celebes at 5.8 by 4.1 metres. Each takes two adults and a child's bed can be added. Fifteen crew look after six guests, with a dining lounge, an al fresco dining area and a foredeck of loungers.

She sails the same year as her sister Silolona, following the monsoons: Komodo, Flores and Alor from May to September, then Raja Ampat, Tribal Papua, Cenderawasih Bay and the Banda Islands from October to April. Silolona Sojourns also pairs her with its restored 164-year-old clan house on the slopes of Gunung Sesean in Toraja.
why: Fifteen crew for six guests is a rare ratio even among private phinisis, and three cabins of near equal size suit three couples or a family without anyone drawing the short straw.

Silolona Sojourns has chartered in these waters for 30 years; its partners include the marine scientists who used Silolona and Si Datu Bua to survey whale sharks, leatherback turtles and oceanic mantas from Cenderawasih Bay to Misool.

faqs: How much does it cost to charter Si Datu Bua?
Silolona Sojourns does not publish rates. She is chartered whole for up to six adults, and the price is quoted for each route and date. Ask James for a quote.
How many guests does Si Datu Bua take?
Six adults, two in each of her three king suites: Banda, the master, and Toraja and Celebes. A child's extra bed can be added to every suite. She has a crew of 15.
What is the difference between Si Datu Bua and Silolona?

Both are Silolona Sojourns phinisis built by Konjo boat builders. Silolona, launched in 2004, is 50 metres with five cabins for ten adults and 17 crew; Si Datu Bua, the newer, is 40.2 metres with three king suites for six and 15 crew.
Where and when does Si Datu Bua sail?
Silolona Sojourns follows the monsoons: Komodo, Flores and Alor from May to September; Raja Ampat, Tribal Papua, Cenderawasih Bay and the Banda Islands from October to April.
Diving, snorkelling, kayaking, paddleboarding, waterskiing, wakeboarding and sport fishing are part of life aboard Silolona Sojourns' yachts, and its crew includes a PADI dive instructor.
Yes. Silolona Sojourns pairs Si Datu Bua with its restored 164-year-old clan house on the slopes of Gunung Sesean in Toraja, Sulawesi. James can plan the two together.
